label: SEGA
summary: Sega Corporation is a Japanese video game company and subsidiary of Sega Sammy Holdings headquartered in Tokyo. It produces several multi-million-selling game franchises for arcades and consoles, including Sonic the Hedgehog, Virtua Fighter, The House of the Dead, and Yakuza. From 1983 until 2001, Sega also developed its own consoles.

label: Sega AM1
summary: Sega AM Research & Development No. 1 is a development department within Sega Corporation that also previously existed as Wow Entertainment and Sega Wow Inc. AM1 spent most of its early existence under the leadership of Rikiya Nakagawa and developed a number of arcade games for Sega, including The House of the Dead series.
focus: Arcade light gun shooters and action games

label: Sega AM2
summary: Sega AM Research & Development No. 2 is a video game development team within Sega. Yu Suzuki, who had previously developed arcade games including Hang-On and Out Run, was the first manager of the department. AM2 is responsible for many of Sega's most iconic arcade franchises including Virtua Fighter, Daytona USA, and After Burner.
focus: Arcade fighting, racing, and simulation games

label: Sega AM3
summary: Sega AM Research & Development No. 3, known as Hitmaker Co., Ltd. from 2000 to 2004, was a division of Sega. Established by 1993, AM3 was managed by Hisao Oguchi and developed a number of arcade games including Virtual On, Sega Rally, Crazy Taxi, and Virtua Tennis.
focus: Arcade racing, mech combat, and sports games

label: Sonic Team
summary: Sega CS R&D Dept. No. 2, doing business as Sonic Team, is a Japanese video game developer owned by Sega. Sonic Team is best known for its Sonic the Hedgehog series. Some Sonic Team games, such as the original Sonic games and Nights into Dreams, are considered among the best video games ever made.
focus: Sonic the Hedgehog franchise and action-platformer games

label: Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio
summary: Sega CS R&D Dept. No. 1, doing business as Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio, is a Japanese video game developer and a division of Sega. Formerly known as Amusement Vision (2000-2004), the studio developed Monkey Ball for arcades. It is now known for developing the Like a Dragon series and the Super Monkey Ball series.
focus: Arcade puzzle games and action-adventure games

label: Smilebit
summary: Sega Sports Research and Development, previously known as Smilebit, was a development division of Sega. One of nine semi-autonomous studios Sega established in 2000, Smilebit was known for its sports simulation titles and Jet Set Radio. Previously known as R&D6 or AM6.

label: United Game Artists
summary: United Game Artists (UGA) was a Japanese video game development division of Sega. Formed from Sega AM9, UGA was known for developing innovative rhythm and action games including Space Channel 5 and Rez. The studio was merged into Sonic Team in 2003.

label: Sega System 16
summary: The Sega System 16 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1985. It was one of Sega's most successful and widely used arcade platforms, powering numerous classic titles. The board used a Motorola 68000 CPU and featured advanced sprite scaling and rotation capabilities for its era.
notableFeatures: Motorola 68000 CPU, hardware sprite scaling, tilemap graphics

label: Sega System 24
summary: The Sega System 24 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1988. It featured improved graphics capabilities over the System 16, with support for higher resolution displays and more complex sprite handling. Used for games like Gain Ground and Bonanza Bros.
notableFeatures: Dual 68000 CPUs, higher resolution display, floppy disk loading

label: Sega System 32
summary: The Sega System 32 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1990. It was one of the most powerful 2D arcade boards of its time, capable of advanced sprite scaling, rotation, and multi-layer scrolling effects. Notable for being one of the first boards to display Sonic the Hedgehog.
notableFeatures: NEC V60 CPU, advanced 2D sprite effects, multi-layer scrolling

label: Sega X Board
summary: The Sega X Board is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1987. It was capable of surface and sprite rotation, enabling pseudo-3D effects for fast-paced action games. The board powered several of Sega's most iconic taikan (body sensation) motion simulator arcade cabinets.
notableFeatures: Sprite rotation, surface scaling, taikan motion cabinet support

label: Sega Y Board
summary: The Sega Y Board is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1988. An enhanced successor to the X Board, it featured improved sprite scaling and rotation capabilities. The board was used in Sega's most ambitious taikan arcade cabinets of the late 1980s.
notableFeatures: Enhanced sprite scaling, 3D rotation effects, 60fps capability

label: Sega Model 1
summary: The Sega Model 1 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1992. It was the first arcade board capable of rendering fully textured 3D polygon graphics in real-time, developed under the guidance of Yu Suzuki. It pioneered the use of 3D graphics in arcade games with Virtua Racing and Virtua Fighter.
notableFeatures: First real-time 3D polygon rendering, custom DSPs, flat-shaded polygons

label: Sega Model 2
summary: The Sega Model 2 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1993, co-developed with Martin Marietta. It was the most powerful arcade hardware of its generation, capable of rendering texture-mapped 3D polygons with filtering. The board powered many of the most commercially successful arcade games of the mid-1990s.
notableFeatures: Texture-mapped 3D, bilinear filtering, 300K+ polygons/sec

label: Sega Model 3
summary: The Sega Model 3 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1996, co-developed with Lockheed Martin. It was the most powerful arcade hardware available at the time of its release, capable of rendering over one million polygons per second with real-time lighting and environmental mapping.
notableFeatures: 1M+ polygons/sec, real-time lighting, environment mapping, PowerPC CPU

label: Sega ST-V
summary: The Sega Titan Video (ST-V) is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1994. Based on the same hardware as the Sega Saturn console, it allowed easy porting between arcade and home platforms. The board was a cost-effective solution for 2D and early 3D arcade games.
notableFeatures: Saturn-compatible hardware, dual SH-2 CPUs, cost-effective development

label: Sega NAOMI
summary: The Sega NAOMI (New Arcade Operation Machine for Interactive) is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1998. Based on the same architecture as the Dreamcast console, it became one of the most commercially successful arcade platforms ever produced, with over 170 games released for the system.
notableFeatures: Dreamcast-compatible, PowerVR2 GPU, GD-ROM media, network support

label: Sega NAOMI 2
summary: The Sega NAOMI 2 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 2000. An enhanced version of the NAOMI, it features dual PowerVR2 GPUs for improved 3D graphics performance, enabling more detailed character models and environments in arcade games.
notableFeatures: Dual PowerVR2 GPUs, T&L engine, enhanced polygon performance

label: Sega Chihiro
summary: The Sega Chihiro is an arcade system board released by Sega in 2002. Based on the Microsoft Xbox hardware architecture, it allowed Sega to leverage Xbox development tools and enabled straightforward porting between arcade and console platforms.
notableFeatures: Xbox-based architecture, nVidia GPU, Ethernet networking

label: Sega Lindbergh
summary: The Sega Lindbergh is an arcade system board released by Sega in 2005. It is a PC-based arcade platform using Intel Pentium 4 processors and nVidia GeForce graphics, marking Sega's transition to commodity PC hardware for arcade systems.
notableFeatures: PC-based architecture, Intel Pentium 4, nVidia GeForce GPU

label: VCO Object
summary: The VCO Object is an early arcade system board released by Sega in 1981. It used a Z80 CPU with custom sprite scaling hardware to create pseudo-3D effects, making it a predecessor to Sega's later Super Scaler technology. Used in Turbo and Buck Rogers: Planet of Zoom.
notableFeatures: Z80 CPU, sprite scaling hardware, pseudo-3D effects

label: Sega G80
summary: The Sega G80 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1981. Available in both raster and vector display variants, the G80 used a Z80 CPU and supported Convert-A-Game kits for economical game swaps. Used for Star Trek: Strategic Operations Simulator and related early Sega arcade titles.
notableFeatures: Z80 CPU, raster and vector variants, Convert-A-Game support

label: Sega Laserdisc
summary: The Sega Laserdisc system is an arcade platform released by Sega in 1983. It combined laserdisc video playback with sprite-based gameplay overlaid on pre-recorded video backgrounds, using a Pioneer laserdisc player. Used for Astron Belt, one of the first laserdisc arcade games.
notableFeatures: Laserdisc playback, Pioneer player, sprite overlay on video

label: Sega System 1
summary: The Sega System 1 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1983. It was Sega's first standard reusable arcade board, using a Z80 CPU. It powered early Sega arcade titles including Flicky, Wonder Boy, and Choplifter.
notableFeatures: Z80 CPU, first standard reusable Sega arcade board, tilemap graphics

label: Sega System 2
summary: The Sega System 2 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1985. An enhanced version of the System 1, it featured improved sound capabilities with dual SN76489 sound chips. Used for Wonder Boy in Monster Land.
notableFeatures: Enhanced System 1, dual SN76489 sound chips, Z80 CPU

label: Sega System 18
summary: The Sega System 18 is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1989. An improved successor to the System 16, it featured an enhanced color palette and additional graphical capabilities. Used for Shadow Dancer and Alien Storm.
notableFeatures: System 16 successor, improved color palette, Motorola 68000 CPU

label: Sega System C
summary: The Sega System C is an arcade system board released by Sega in 1990. Based on the Mega Drive/Genesis hardware architecture, it served as a cost-effective arcade platform for 2D games. The arcade version of Columns ran on this board.
notableFeatures: Mega Drive-based arcade hardware, cost-effective, 2D-focused

label: Sega Pre-System 1
summary: Pre-System 1 refers to Sega's early custom discrete arcade boards used before the standardized System 1. Games like Zaxxon, Pengo, and Congo Bongo ran on dedicated hardware specific to each game, before Sega adopted reusable platform boards.
notableFeatures: Custom discrete boards, game-specific hardware, Z80-based

label: Sega ALLS
summary: The Sega ALLS is a modern arcade system platform released by Sega in 2018. Based on Windows 10 IoT with Unreal Engine 4 support, it represents Sega's current generation of PC-based arcade hardware. Used for House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn.
notableFeatures: Windows 10 IoT, Unreal Engine 4 support, PC-based

label: Sega Super Scaler
summary: Sega's first Super Scaler arcade system board (1985), initially known as 'Sega Hang-On hardware'. Featured dual Motorola 68000 processors and hardware sprite scaling for pseudo-3D effects. A refinement of the earlier VCO Object hardware, it powered Hang-On and Space Harrier.
notableFeatures: Dual Motorola 68000, hardware sprite scaling, pseudo-3D

label: Sega OutRun Hardware
summary: Second-generation Super Scaler arcade board (1986), based on the System 16 architecture. Designed because Yu Suzuki needed more powerful hardware for Out Run's advanced road rendering and sprite scaling effects. Featured enhanced graphical capabilities over the original Super Scaler hardware.
notableFeatures: System 16-based, enhanced sprite scaling, road rendering

label: Hang-On
summary: Hang-On is a 1985 racing video game developed and published by Sega for arcades. It was one of the first arcade games to use 16-bit graphics and uses the Super Scaler arcade system board. The deluxe cabinet version introduced a motion-controlled arcade cabinet where the player sits on a large motorbike-shaped cabinet.

label: Space Harrier
summary: Space Harrier is a 1985 rail shooter video game developed and published by Sega for arcades. The arcade game is controlled by an analog flight stick while the deluxe cabinet is a cockpit-style motion simulator cabinet that pitches and rolls during play, referred to as a taikan arcade game in Japan.

label: Fantasy Zone
summary: Fantasy Zone is a 1986 shoot 'em up video game developed and published by Sega for arcades on the System 16 hardware. The player controls a sentient spaceship named Opa-Opa through colorful, surreal stages. Known for its distinctive bright pastel aesthetic and shopping mechanic.

label: Out Run
summary: Out Run is a 1986 racing video game developed and published by Sega for arcades. It is known for its pioneering hardware and graphics, nonlinear gameplay, a selectable soundtrack with music composed by Hiroshi Kawaguchi, and the hydraulic motion simulator deluxe arcade cabinet.

label: Alex Kidd: The Lost Stars
summary: Alex Kidd: The Lost Stars is a 1986 platformer video game developed and published by Sega for arcades on the System 16 hardware. An early entry in the Alex Kidd franchise, it tasks players with recovering stolen celestial bodies across multiple themed worlds.

label: Quartet
summary: Quartet is a 1986 run-and-gun arcade game developed and published by Sega for the System 16 hardware. It supports up to four simultaneous players, each controlling a different character fighting through side-scrolling levels filled with enemies and bosses.

label: Shinobi
summary: Shinobi is a 1987 hack and slash video game developed and published by Sega for arcades on the Sega System 16 board. The player controls ninja Joe Musashi, who must stop the Zeed terrorist organization from kidnapping students of his clan.

label: After Burner
summary: After Burner is a 1987 rail shooter video game developed by Sega and published for arcades. The player controls an American F-14 Tomcat fighter jet. It runs on the Sega X Board arcade system and features an elaborate hydraulic taikan motion simulator arcade cabinet.

label: Thunder Blade
summary: Thunder Blade is a 1987 helicopter combat arcade game developed and published by Sega on the X Board hardware. Players pilot an attack helicopter through urban and military environments, alternating between top-down and third-person perspectives.

label: Super Hang-On
summary: Super Hang-On is a 1987 motorcycle racing arcade game developed and published by Sega on the X Board hardware. The sequel to Hang-On, it features improved graphics, a turbo boost mechanic, and multiple course options spanning different world regions.

label: Altered Beast
summary: Altered Beast is a 1988 beat 'em up video game developed by Team Shinobi and published by Sega for arcades. Set in Ancient Greece, the game follows a Roman centurion resurrected by Zeus to rescue his daughter Athena. By collecting power-ups, the player can transform into one of five mythical beasts.

label: Power Drift
summary: Power Drift is a 1988 racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega on the Y Board hardware. Players race go-karts across fantastical rollercoaster-like tracks with dramatic elevation changes and elaborate sprite-scaling 3D effects.

label: Galaxy Force II
summary: Galaxy Force II is a 1988 rail shooter arcade game developed and published by Sega on the Y Board hardware. Players pilot a spaceship through various planetary environments with pseudo-3D graphics. The deluxe cabinet was one of Sega's largest and most elaborate motion simulators.

label: Gain Ground
summary: Gain Ground is a 1988 action-strategy arcade game developed and published by Sega on the System 24 hardware. Players rescue captive warriors across historically-themed stages, building up a roster of characters with unique weapons and abilities.

label: Golden Axe
summary: Golden Axe is a 1989 beat 'em up video game developed and published by Sega for arcades on the Sega System 16B hardware. Players control one of three warriors who must free the fantasy land of Yuria from the tyrannical rule of Death Adder, who wields the titular Golden Axe.

label: Columns
summary: Columns is a match-three puzzle video game originally developed by Jay Geertsen and released commercially by Sega in 1989. Sega ported the game to arcades on the System 16 hardware and then to several Sega consoles, positioning it as a competitor to Tetris.

label: Bonanza Bros.
summary: Bonanza Bros. is a 1990 action arcade game developed and published by Sega on the System 24 hardware. Players control two bumbling burglars who must infiltrate various buildings to collect treasures while avoiding guards. The game features a distinctive split-screen cooperative mode.

label: G-LOC: Air Battle
summary: G-LOC: Air Battle is a 1990 combat flight arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega on the Y Board hardware. A spiritual successor to After Burner, it features a first-person cockpit view and was designed for Sega's R360 rotating arcade cabinet.

label: Rad Mobile
summary: Rad Mobile is a 1991 racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega on the System 32 hardware. Notable for being the first video game to feature Sonic the Hedgehog, who appears as a rearview mirror ornament. The game features realistic weather effects and day-night transitions.

label: Virtua Racing
summary: Virtua Racing is a 1992 Formula One racing video game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega for arcades. It was initially a proof-of-concept application for exercising the Model 1, a new 3D graphics platform then under development. The results were so encouraging that it was fully developed into a standalone arcade title.

label: Golden Axe: The Revenge of Death Adder
summary: Golden Axe: The Revenge of Death Adder is a 1992 beat 'em up arcade game developed and published by Sega on the System 32 hardware. The sequel to Golden Axe features four new playable characters and improved graphics. It was only released as an arcade game and never ported to home consoles.

label: Virtua Fighter
summary: Virtua Fighter is a 1993 fighting game developed and published by Sega for arcades. Developed for the Sega Model 1 by AM2 under Yu Suzuki, it was the first arcade fighting game to feature fully 3D polygon graphics. It pioneered the 3D fighting game genre.

label: SegaSonic the Hedgehog
summary: SegaSonic the Hedgehog is a 1993 arcade platformer developed by Sega AM3 and Sonic Team, running on the System 32 hardware. Controlled with a trackball, it features Sonic, Ray, and Mighty navigating isometric obstacle courses. One of the few Sonic games developed exclusively for arcades.

label: Daytona USA
summary: Daytona USA is a 1994 racing game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega for arcades. Inspired by the popularity of NASCAR, it has players race stock cars on one of three courses. It was the first game released on the Sega Model 2 arcade system board and became one of the highest-grossing arcade games.

label: Virtua Cop
summary: Virtua Cop is a 1994 light gun shooter video game developed and published by Sega for arcades on the Model 2 system. Players take on the role of police officers fighting crime using light guns, with fully 3D polygon environments and enemies.

label: Virtua Fighter 2
summary: Virtua Fighter 2 is a 1994 fighting game developed and published by Sega for arcades. Created by Sega's Yu Suzuki-headed AM2 team on the Sega Model 2 hardware, it provided a significant upgrade in graphical capabilities over the original, with texture-mapped characters and 60fps gameplay.

label: Virtua Striker
summary: Virtua Striker is a 1994 football/soccer arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega on the Model 2 hardware. It was one of the first 3D football games, featuring fast-paced arcade-style gameplay with international teams.

label: Sega Rally Championship
summary: Sega Rally Championship is a 1995 racing game developed and published by Sega. Originally released for arcades using the Model 2 board, it simulates driving on different surfaces with varying friction. As the first racing game to incorporate this feature, it is considered a milestone in the evolution of the racing game genre.

label: Fighting Vipers
summary: Fighting Vipers is a 1995 fighting video game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega for arcades on the Model 2. A 3D fighter using the same engine as Virtua Fighter 2, it features enclosed arenas and an armor mechanic, targeting Western audiences with a more freeform fighting style.

label: Manx TT Superbike
summary: Manx TT Superbike is a 1995 motorcycle racing arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the Model 2 hardware. Based on the famous Isle of Man TT race, it features two courses and a distinctive motorcycle-shaped cabinet with handlebar controls.

label: Virtual-On
summary: Cyber Troopers Virtual-On is a 1995 mech combat video game developed by Sega AM3 on the Model 2 hardware. Players control large robots called Virtuaroids in fast-paced arena battles. The arcade cabinet featured distinctive twin-stick controls that became iconic.

label: Virtua Cop 2
summary: Virtua Cop 2 is a 1995 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Model 2 hardware. The sequel to Virtua Cop, it features branching paths, more detailed 3D environments, and cooperative two-player gameplay.

label: Sonic the Fighters
summary: Sonic the Fighters is a 1996 fighting arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Model 2 hardware. Featuring characters from the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise in 3D arena combat, it uses a simplified version of the Fighting Vipers engine.

label: Last Bronx
summary: Last Bronx is a 1996 weapons-based fighting arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the Model 2 hardware. Set in a near-future Tokyo, characters fight with real-world weapons in 3D arenas. It was later ported to the Sega Saturn.

label: Die Hard Arcade
summary: Die Hard Arcade, known in Japan as Dynamite Deka, is a 1996 3D beat 'em up arcade game developed by Sega AM1. Players fight through a skyscraper to rescue hostages. The game was released on the Sega Model 2 and Sega ST-V arcade boards.

label: Gunblade NY
summary: Gunblade NY is a 1996 light gun rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the Model 2 hardware. Players ride in a helicopter and shoot enemies across New York City, using a mounted machine gun controller in the arcade cabinet.

label: Wave Runner
summary: Wave Runner is a 1996 jet ski racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Model 2 hardware. Players race personal watercraft across various ocean courses with realistic wave physics and water spray effects.

label: Decathlete
summary: Decathlete is a 1996 sports arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the ST-V hardware. Players compete in ten track and field events including sprints, hurdles, javelin throw, and high jump. Known internationally as Athlete Kings.

label: Scud Race
summary: Scud Race, known as Sega Super GT in North America, is a 1996 racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Model 3 hardware. Players race sports cars including a Porsche 911, Ferrari F40, and Dodge Viper across four courses. It was one of the first Model 3 titles.

label: Virtua Fighter 3
summary: Virtua Fighter 3 is a 1996 fighting video game developed by Sega AM2 on the Model 3 hardware. The third main installment in the Virtua Fighter series, it introduced uneven terrain stages and a new dodge button mechanic. It featured unprecedented graphical detail for its time.

label: The House of the Dead
summary: The House of the Dead is a 1997 light gun shooter video game developed by Sega AM1 and published by Sega for arcades on the Model 2 hardware. Players combat an army of undead experiments created by a mad scientist. It launched one of Sega's most enduring arcade franchises.

label: Spikeout
summary: Spikeout is a 1998 beat 'em up arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Model 3 hardware. Up to four players fight through urban environments in cooperative 3D brawling action. It was one of the last major titles on the Model 3 platform.

label: Daytona USA 2
summary: Daytona USA 2: Battle on the Edge is a 1998 racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Model 3 hardware. The sequel to Daytona USA features improved graphics, new courses, and enhanced multiplayer capabilities with linkable cabinets.

label: Sega Rally 2
summary: Sega Rally 2 is a 1998 rally racing arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the Model 3 hardware. The sequel to Sega Rally Championship features more cars, longer courses, and improved surface physics with dynamic weather conditions.

label: The Ocean Hunter
summary: The Ocean Hunter is a 1998 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the Model 3 hardware. Players hunt giant sea monsters in an underwater adventure using harpoon gun controllers, featuring impressive underwater 3D environments.

label: The House of the Dead 2
summary: The House of the Dead 2 is a 1998 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the NAOMI hardware. The sequel to The House of the Dead features improved 3D graphics, branching paths, and a new cast of characters fighting a zombie outbreak in Venice, Italy.

label: Virtual-On Oratorio Tangram
summary: Virtual-On Oratorio Tangram is a 1998 mech combat arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the NAOMI hardware. The sequel to Virtual-On, it features faster gameplay, new Virtuaroid mechs, and refined twin-stick controls.

label: Dynamite Cop
summary: Dynamite Cop, known in Japan as Dynamite Deka 2, is a 1998 3D beat 'em up arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the NAOMI hardware. The sequel to Die Hard Arcade features players fighting terrorists aboard a cruise ship with an arsenal of improvised weapons.

label: Crazy Taxi
summary: Crazy Taxi is a racing video game developed and published by Sega. First released in arcades in 1999 on NAOMI hardware, gameplay is based on picking up taxi customers and driving to their destination as quickly as possible. It became one of Sega's most commercially successful arcade franchises.

label: Virtua Tennis
summary: Virtua Tennis is a 1999 tennis simulation arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the NAOMI hardware. It features accessible pick-up-and-play mechanics with real professional tennis players. The game launched a successful multi-platform series.

label: Derby Owners Club
summary: Derby Owners Club is a 1999 horse racing simulation arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the NAOMI hardware. Players breed, train, and race virtual horses using an IC card save system, allowing them to develop their stable over multiple play sessions.

label: Samba de Amigo
summary: Samba de Amigo is a 1999 rhythm arcade game developed by Sonic Team on the NAOMI hardware. Players shake maraca controllers in time with Latin and pop music. Its colorful presentation and unique motion controls made it a standout arcade attraction.

label: Jambo! Safari
summary: Jambo! Safari is a 1999 driving and lasso arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the NAOMI hardware. Players drive a jeep through African savanna landscapes, using a lasso to capture wild animals for wildlife conservation. The cabinet features a unique steering wheel with integrated lasso trigger.

label: Monkey Ball
summary: Monkey Ball is a 2001 arcade game developed by Amusement Vision (now Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio) and published by Sega on NAOMI hardware. Players tilt the stage to guide a monkey in a transparent ball through obstacle courses. It was controlled with a distinctive banana-shaped analog stick and later ported as Super Monkey Ball for the GameCube.

label: Initial D Arcade Stage
summary: Initial D Arcade Stage is a 2002 arcade racing game series developed by Sega, based on the anime and manga series Initial D. Players race modified Japanese cars through mountain passes, with an IC card system to save car tuning progress.

label: Virtua Fighter 4
summary: Virtua Fighter 4 is a 2001 fighting arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the NAOMI 2 hardware. The fourth main installment features two new characters, refined game mechanics, and an innovative ranking system using IC cards to track player statistics.

label: Virtua Striker 3
summary: Virtua Striker 3 is a 2001 football/soccer arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the NAOMI 2 hardware. The third installment features improved 3D graphics, more teams, and refined arcade-style gameplay.

label: Virtua Tennis 2
summary: Virtua Tennis 2, known as Power Smash 2 in Japan, is a 2001 tennis simulation arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the NAOMI 2 hardware. It features an expanded roster of real tennis players and improved graphics over the original.

label: The House of the Dead III
summary: The House of the Dead III is a 2002 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the Chihiro hardware. Set in a post-apocalyptic future, players use shotguns instead of pistols. It was one of the first titles on the Xbox-based Chihiro arcade board.

label: OutRun 2
summary: OutRun 2 is a 2003 racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Chihiro hardware. A long-awaited sequel to the 1986 classic, it retains the branching course design and selectable soundtrack while featuring fully 3D Ferrari sports cars and scenic routes.

label: Virtua Cop 3
summary: Virtua Cop 3 is a 2003 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Chihiro hardware. The third installment in the Virtua Cop series features a bullet-time mechanic and fully 3D environments with destructible elements.

label: The House of the Dead 4
summary: The House of the Dead 4 is a 2005 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the Lindbergh hardware. It features submachine gun controllers with shake-activated grenade attacks, set three years after the events of the second game.

label: Virtua Fighter 5
summary: Virtua Fighter 5 is a 2006 fighting arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Lindbergh hardware. The fifth main installment introduced two new characters and featured the most detailed character models and stages in the series at the time of release.

label: After Burner Climax
summary: After Burner Climax is a 2006 rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the Lindbergh hardware. A modern update of the After Burner series, it features a climax gauge mechanic for bullet-time targeting and branching mission paths.

label: Let's Go Jungle!
summary: Let's Go Jungle! Lost on the Island of Spice is a 2006 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the Lindbergh hardware. Two players cooperate to survive giant insect attacks on a tropical island, using a shared booth-style cabinet.

label: Confidential Mission
summary: Confidential Mission is a 2000 light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the NAOMI hardware. Players take on the role of secret agents fighting a global terrorist organization, featuring James Bond-inspired spy thriller gameplay.

label: Sega Marine Fishing
summary: Sega Marine Fishing is a 1999 fishing simulation arcade game developed by Sega AM3 on the NAOMI hardware. Players use a rod-shaped controller to catch various species of fish in tropical marine environments with colorful underwater graphics.

label: Turbo
summary: Turbo is a 1981 racing arcade game developed and published by Sega on the VCO Object hardware. One of the earliest racing games to feature full-color sprite-based graphics and a rear-view perspective, it was one of Sega's first major arcade hits. Features varied terrain including cities, tunnels, and seaside roads.

label: Buck Rogers: Planet of Zoom
summary: Buck Rogers: Planet of Zoom is a 1982 rail shooter arcade game developed and published by Sega on the VCO Object hardware. A licensed rail shooter based on the Buck Rogers franchise, it used pseudo-3D sprite scaling, making it a precursor to Space Harrier's visual style.

label: Zaxxon
summary: Zaxxon is a 1982 scrolling shooter arcade game developed by Sega and Ikegami Tsushinki. A pioneering isometric-perspective scrolling shooter, it was one of the first games to display shadows to indicate height. Produced over $1 billion in quarters by 1982.

label: Pengo
summary: Pengo is a 1982 maze arcade game developed by Coreland and published by Sega. Players control a penguin pushing ice blocks to crush enemies called Sno-Bees. Featured a popcorn-themed soundtrack and was a commercial success in arcades.

label: Congo Bongo
summary: Congo Bongo is a 1983 platform arcade game developed by Sega and Ikegami Tsushinki. An isometric platformer inspired by Nintendo's Donkey Kong, players navigate through four stages avoiding enemies using isometric perspective similar to Zaxxon.

label: Astron Belt
summary: Astron Belt is a 1983 rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega on the Sega Laserdisc system. One of the first laserdisc video games, it featured pre-recorded video backgrounds with sprite-based gameplay overlaid. Often cited alongside Dragon's Lair as a landmark in arcade laserdisc gaming.

label: Star Trek: Strategic Operations Simulator
summary: Star Trek: Strategic Operations Simulator is a 1983 space combat simulator arcade game developed by Sega Electronics on the G80 vector hardware. Based on the original Star Trek TV series, it uses color vector graphics for both 2D tactical display and 3D first-person view. Featured a deluxe cabinet modeled after the Enterprise bridge chairs.

label: Flicky
summary: Flicky is a 1984 platform arcade game developed and published by Sega on the System 1 hardware. A single-screen platform game where the player controls a blue bird named Flicky rescuing baby chicks from house cats and iguanas. The Flicky characters later appeared in the Sonic the Hedgehog series as the animals freed from Badniks.

label: Choplifter
summary: Choplifter is a 1985 scrolling shooter arcade game. Originally developed by Dan Gorlin for Apple II in 1982, Sega created a reverse port for arcades running on System 1 hardware. Players pilot a helicopter to rescue hostages from enemy territory while battling tanks and jets. Number one table arcade game in Japan, October 1985.

label: Wonder Boy
summary: Wonder Boy is a 1986 platform arcade game developed by Escape and published by Sega on the System 1 hardware. The first entry in the long-running Wonder Boy series, it features a side-scrolling platformer with a health mechanic tied to fruit collection. Inspired Hudson Soft's Adventure Island series.

label: Wonder Boy in Monster Land
summary: Wonder Boy in Monster Land is a 1987 platform/action RPG arcade game developed by Westone and published by Sega on the System 2 hardware. A sequel to Wonder Boy, it introduced RPG elements like shops, equipment, and gold collection. Praised as an innovative arcade/RPG hybrid.

label: Alien Syndrome
summary: Alien Syndrome is a 1987 run and gun arcade game developed by Sega R&D1 on the System 16B hardware. A two-player cooperative game where players rescue hostages from alien-infested spaceships. Third most successful table arcade in Japan, April 1987.

label: Dynamite Düx
summary: Dynamite Düx is a 1988 beat 'em up arcade game developed by Sega R&D8 on the System 16 hardware. A side-scrolling beat 'em up featuring cartoon ducks fighting enemies. Notable for credits linking to Yu Suzuki as producer and Hiroshi Kawaguchi as composer.

label: Galaxy Force
summary: Galaxy Force is a 1988 rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega R&D1 on the Y Board hardware. A third-person rail shooter designed to showcase the Y Board hardware, with rotating scrolling backgrounds and massive sprites. Michael Jackson received a Galaxy Force Super Deluxe cabinet as a gift during his visit to Sega.

label: Cyber Police ESWAT
summary: Cyber Police ESWAT is a 1989 run and gun arcade game developed by Sega R&D1 on the System 16B hardware. A side-scrolling platformer where the player controls a police officer who acquires powerful ICE cybernetic armor mid-game, transforming from a regular cop into an armored cyber warrior.

label: Super Monaco GP
summary: Super Monaco GP is a 1989 racing arcade game developed by Sega on the X Board hardware. A Formula One-style racing game featuring detailed sprite scaling and challenging AI opponents. One of the most popular racing games of the late 1980s arcade era.

label: Shadow Dancer
summary: Shadow Dancer is a 1989 platform/action arcade game developed by Sega on the System 18 hardware. A sequel in the Shinobi series, the arcade version features a ninja accompanied by an attack dog. The first game on Sega System 18 hardware.

label: Alien Storm
summary: Alien Storm is a 1990 beat 'em up arcade game developed by Sega AM1 on the System 18 hardware. A three-player beat 'em up similar to Golden Axe but with a sci-fi setting, combining side-scrolling brawling with first-person shooting sequences. Most successful table arcade in Japan, June 1990.

label: OutRunners
summary: OutRunners is a 1992 racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 on the System 32 hardware. A multiplayer sequel to Out Run allowing up to eight players to compete simultaneously via linked cabinets. Features multiple selectable cars and branching routes.

label: Ollie King
summary: Ollie King is a 2003 skateboarding sports arcade game developed by Smilebit on the Chihiro hardware. Players perform skateboarding tricks and race through courses. Features a soundtrack by Hideki Naganuma with the same funk/electronic style as Jet Set Radio.

label: House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn
summary: House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn is a 2018 rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega on the ALLS hardware. The fifth mainline House of the Dead installment, built on Unreal Engine 4 for Sega's modern PC-based arcade platform. Features up to 200 enemies on screen.

label: Yu Suzuki
summary: Yu Suzuki is a Japanese game designer, producer, programmer, and engineer, who headed Sega's AM2 team for 18 years. Considered one of the first auteurs of video games, he created pioneering arcade hits including Hang-On, Space Harrier, Out Run, After Burner, Virtua Racing, and Virtua Fighter, as well as the critically acclaimed Shenmue series.

label: Toshihiro Nagoshi
summary: Toshihiro Nagoshi is a Japanese video game producer, director, and designer. He was the chief creative officer for Sega until 2021 and the general director of Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio. He joined Sega in 1989 and worked on Daytona USA at AM2 before leading Amusement Vision on Monkey Ball.

label: Yuji Naka
summary: Yuji Naka is a Japanese former video game designer and programmer. He is the co-creator of the Sonic the Hedgehog series and was the president of Sonic Team at Sega until his departure in 2006. His programming work on early arcade and console titles helped establish Sega's technical reputation.
notableRoles: Lead programmer, Director, Sonic Team president

label: Rieko Kodama
summary: Rieko Kodama, also known as Phoenix Rie, was a Japanese video game artist, director, and producer employed by Sega from 1984 until her death in 2022. She is primarily known for her work on the Phantasy Star series and Skies of Arcadia, and is recognized as one of the first successful women in the video game industry.

label: Tetsuya Mizuguchi
summary: Tetsuya Mizuguchi is a Japanese video game designer and producer. He worked at Sega's AM3 division on Sega Rally Championship and other arcade titles before heading United Game Artists, where he directed Space Channel 5 and Rez. He later founded Q Entertainment and Enhance.

label: Hiroshi Kawaguchi
summary: Sega's longest-serving game music composer, joining in 1984. Created the iconic soundtracks for Yu Suzuki's super scaler arcade games including Out Run, Space Harrier, After Burner, and Hang-On. Known by the alias "Hiro" in early game credits.

label: Takenobu Mitsuyoshi
summary: Sega composer and vocalist famous for singing the Daytona USA soundtrack ("Let's Go Away", "Rolling Start"). Joined Sega in 1990 and composed music for many AM2 arcade titles including Virtua Fighter 2 and Virtua Striker. Also provided the voice of Kage-Maru in the Virtua Fighter series.

label: Takayuki Nakamura
summary: Sega AM2 composer (1989–1996) who created the soundtracks for Virtua Fighter and OutRunners. After leaving Sega in 1996, he composed the critically acclaimed Lumines soundtrack. Also contributed sound programming to Streets of Rage.

label: Hisao Oguchi
summary: Head of Sega AM3/Hitmaker who directed Super Monaco GP and Rad Mobile. Joined Sega in 1984 and managed AM3 from 1993, overseeing development of Crazy Taxi, Derby Owners Club, and Virtua Tennis. Became president of Sega in 2003.

label: Naoto Ohshima
summary: Creator of the Sonic the Hedgehog character design. Joined Sega in 1987 and worked as character designer and artist before directing NiGHTS into Dreams and Burning Rangers at Sonic Team. Also designed Dr. Eggman. Left Sega in 1999 to co-found Artoon.

label: Hirokazu Yasuhara
summary: Co-creator of Sonic the Hedgehog who designed the gameplay mechanics and stage layouts for the original Sonic games. Joined Sega in 1988 and directed Sonic 3 and Sonic & Knuckles. Left Sega in 1999, later worked at Naughty Dog on the Uncharted series.

label: Takashi Iizuka
summary: Current head of Sonic Team since 2008. Lead game designer of NiGHTS into Dreams and director of Sonic Adventure and Sonic Adventure 2. Joined Sega in 1992 and has been the custodian of the Sonic franchise for over two decades.
notableRoles: Game Designer, Director, Sonic Team Head (2008–present)

label: Jun Senoue
summary: Sonic Team composer and guitarist of the band Crush 40. Lead composer for the Sonic Adventure series, known for the rock-influenced Sonic soundtracks. Joined Sega in 1993. Also contributed music to Sega Rally 2.

label: Kazuyuki Hoshino
summary: Sonic Team's creative director who designed iconic characters including Metal Sonic, Amy Rose, Shadow the Hedgehog, and the Chao. Joined Sega in 1991 and served as art director for the Sonic Adventure series.
notableRoles: Creative Director, Character Designer, Art Director

label: Shun Nakamura
summary: Sonic Team game designer who directed Samba de Amigo (arcade) and Billy Hatcher and the Giant Egg. Joined Sega around 1997 and worked as field designer on Sonic Adventure before taking director roles on original Sonic Team IPs.

label: Tomoya Ohtani
summary: Sonic Team's lead composer since Sonic the Hedgehog (2006), creating iconic soundtracks for the modern Sonic era including Sonic Unleashed, Sonic Colors, and Sonic Frontiers. Joined Sega in 1999.

label: Hideki Naganuma
summary: Composer and DJ famous for Jet Set Radio's groundbreaking funk/hip-hop/electronic soundtrack. Joined Sega in 1998 and worked at Smilebit. Also composed music for Ollie King (arcade) and Sonic Rush. Left Sega in 2008.

label: Masayoshi Yokoyama
summary: Current head of Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio since 2021 and key developer of the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series. Started at Sega in 1999 as a planner on Jet Set Radio before becoming central to the Yakuza franchise as scenario writer, producer, and ultimately studio head.
notableRoles: Director, Producer, Writer, RGG Studio Head (2021–present)

label: Richard Jacques
summary: British composer who worked at Sega Europe from 1994 to 2004. Known for Sonic R's vocal soundtrack ("Can You Feel the Sunshine"), Jet Set Radio, and Headhunter. The only non-Japanese creator in this research set.

label: Mie Kumagai
summary: Japanese video game producer and director at Sega AM3/Hitmaker. She became the first female president of a Japanese video game company when she took over as head of Hitmaker. Produced Virtua Tennis, Derby Owners Club, and Gunblade NY, and directed Confidential Mission.

label: Compile
summary: Compile Co., Ltd. was a Japanese video game developer founded by Masamitsu Niitani in 1982. The company was best known for creating the Puyo Puyo puzzle game series and for developing numerous shoot-'em-up games. Compile went bankrupt in 2003, and the Puyo Puyo intellectual property was acquired by Sega.

label: Westone Bit Entertainment
summary: Westone Bit Entertainment, originally known as Escape, was a Japanese video game developer founded in 1986. The company is best known for creating the Wonder Boy and Monster World series for Sega arcade hardware and consoles. Westone closed in 2014.

label: Sega Rosso
summary: Sega Rosso was a Japanese video game development studio and subsidiary of Sega. Established in 2000, Sega Rosso developed the Initial D Arcade Stage series, one of the most successful racing arcade franchises in Japan. The studio was dissolved in 2003 and merged into Sega's Hitmaker subsidiary.

label: Sega AM4
summary: Sega AM Research & Development No. 4 was an arcade game development division of Sega, established in 1993. AM4 developed racing and sports arcade games. The division was restructured in 2000 and reorganized into Amusement Vision, which later became Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio.

label: Sega Hikaru
summary: The Sega Hikaru is an arcade system board released by Sega in 2000. Based on the NAOMI architecture, the Hikaru featured a custom 3D GPU capable of advanced real-time phong shading effects. It was used for a small number of visually ambitious arcade titles including Planet Harriers and Brave Firefighters.
notableFeatures: NAOMI-based, custom 3D GPU, real-time phong shading

label: Sega RingEdge
summary: The Sega RingEdge is a PC-based arcade system board released by Sega in 2009. It uses an Intel Celeron processor and NVIDIA GeForce GPU running Windows Embedded. The RingEdge was designed as an affordable, compact arcade platform and was used for games such as Border Break and Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade.
notableFeatures: Intel Celeron, NVIDIA GeForce, Windows Embedded

label: Sega RingEdge 2
summary: The Sega RingEdge 2 is an upgraded PC-based arcade system board released by Sega in 2011. Featuring an Intel Core i3/i5 processor and improved NVIDIA GPU running Windows Embedded, it offered greater processing power than its predecessor. It was used for rhythm games such as Maimai.
notableFeatures: Intel Core i3/i5, improved NVIDIA GPU, Windows Embedded

label: Sega Nu
summary: The Sega Nu is a PC-based arcade system board released by Sega in 2013. Powered by an Intel Core i-series processor and NVIDIA GeForce GTX GPU, the Nu represented a significant performance step up from earlier PC-based boards. It was used for modern arcade titles including Chunithm, Kantai Collection Arcade, and Ongeki.
notableFeatures: Intel Core i-series, NVIDIA GeForce GTX

label: Sega Europa-R
summary: The Sega Europa-R is a budget PC-based arcade system board released by Sega in 2007. Using an AMD Athlon processor and ATI Radeon GPU, the Europa-R served as a lower-cost alternative to the Lindbergh platform. It was used for racing titles such as Sega Rally 3 and Sega Race TV.
notableFeatures: AMD Athlon, ATI Radeon, budget Lindbergh successor

label: Periscope
summary: Periscope is an electro-mechanical arcade game manufactured by Sega and released in 1966. The player looks through a periscope viewfinder and fires torpedoes at moving cardboard ships illuminated by backlighting. It was one of the first arcade games to cost a quarter per play and became a major international hit, establishing Sega as a leading arcade manufacturer.

label: Heavyweight Champ
summary: Heavyweight Champ is a boxing arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1976. Considered one of the first fighting games, it uses two joysticks to control a boxer's punches — high and low. The game was remade by Sega in 1987 as a more advanced version using the System 16 hardware.

label: Head On
summary: Head On is an arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1979. The player drives a car around a maze-like track collecting dots while avoiding an opposing car. It is considered a precursor to Pac-Man and was one of the earliest dot-eating maze games, becoming a major arcade hit worldwide.

label: Monaco GP
summary: Monaco GP is a top-down racing arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1979. Built with discrete logic circuits rather than a microprocessor, the game features scrolling road gameplay where the player must avoid other cars while racing. It was one of the highest-grossing arcade games of 1979 and 1980.

label: Deep Scan
summary: Deep Scan is a fixed shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1979. The player controls a destroyer on the ocean surface, dropping depth charges to destroy submarines below. It was an early example of depth-based gameplay mechanics in arcade games.

label: Carnival
summary: Carnival is a gallery shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1980. The player shoots at rows of moving targets including rabbits, ducks, and owls using a limited supply of bullets. It was one of Sega's early hits and featured a distinctive musical theme that played during gameplay.

label: Frogger
summary: Frogger is an action arcade game developed by Konami and manufactured by Sega for the North American market, released in 1981. The player guides a frog across a busy road and a hazardous river to reach home. Frogger became one of the most iconic arcade games of the golden age and has spawned numerous sequels.

label: Astro Blaster
summary: Astro Blaster is a fixed shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1981. Running on the Sega G80 hardware, the player defends against waves of alien attackers while managing a limited fuel supply. The game featured digitized speech, which was a notable technical achievement at the time.

label: Space Fury
summary: Space Fury is a multidirectional shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1981. Running on the Sega G80 vector hardware, the player battles alien ships and can dock with defeated enemies to upgrade their spacecraft. It was one of the first arcade games to feature synthesized speech directed at the player.

label: Subroc-3D
summary: Subroc-3D is a shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1982. Using the Sega G80 hardware with a special rotating periscope-like viewer, it was one of the first arcade games to feature true stereoscopic 3D visuals. The player battles submarines and aircraft in a first-person perspective.

label: Tac/Scan
summary: Tac/Scan is a multidirectional shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1982. Running on the Sega G80 vector hardware, the player controls a squadron of ships in a formation-based space combat game. It was notable for its innovative squadron-management mechanics.

label: Champion Boxing
summary: Champion Boxing is a sports/fighting arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1984, running on the System 1 hardware. It is notable as the first game designed by Yu Suzuki at Sega. The player controls a boxer in a side-view ring, using different punch and dodge moves to defeat opponents.

label: Bank Panic
summary: Bank Panic is a shooter arcade game developed by Sanritsu and released by Sega in 1984 on the System 1 hardware. The player is a sheriff protecting a bank with twelve doors, shooting bandits while avoiding customers. The game's frantic multi-door gameplay made it a notable title of the early Sega arcade era.

label: My Hero
summary: My Hero is a beat 'em up arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1985 on the System 1 hardware. The player fights through urban streets to rescue a kidnapped girlfriend, using punches and kicks against waves of enemies. Known in Japan as Seishun Scandal.

label: Teddy Boy Blues
summary: Teddy Boy Blues is a platformer arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1985 on the System 1 hardware. Named after a Japanese pop song, the player shoots enemies that shrink into collectible items. The game was later ported to the Sega Master System.

label: Ninja Princess
summary: Ninja Princess, also known as Sega Ninja, is a run and gun arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1985 on the System 1 hardware. The player controls a ninja princess throwing shurikens at enemies while navigating scrolling stages. It was later released on the Master System as The Ninja.

label: Enduro Racer
summary: Enduro Racer is a racing arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1986 using the Super Scaler hardware. Designed by Yu Suzuki, the player rides a dirt bike over hills and obstacles in a pseudo-3D perspective similar to Hang-On. The game featured a motorcycle-shaped cabinet that players would lean on to steer.

label: Action Fighter
summary: Action Fighter is a vertically scrolling shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1986 on the System 16 hardware. The player controls a transforming vehicle that can switch between a motorcycle, a car, and a jet. The game combined shoot-'em-up action with vehicular combat.

label: SDI: Strategic Defense Initiative
summary: SDI: Strategic Defense Initiative is a shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1987 on the System 16 hardware. Inspired by the real-world Strategic Defense Initiative, the player uses a trackball to aim and destroy incoming missiles and enemy satellites in a Cold War-themed setting.

label: Scramble Spirits
summary: Scramble Spirits is a vertically scrolling shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1988 on the System 16 hardware. Inspired by Capcom's 1942, the player flies a World War II-era fighter plane through multiple stages of aerial combat. The game featured a two-player cooperative mode.

label: Turbo Out Run
summary: Turbo Out Run is a racing arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1989, running on the OutRun dedicated hardware. A sequel to Out Run, it features a cross-country race from New York to Los Angeles with a turbo boost mechanic. The game added weather effects and vehicle upgrades between stages.

label: Wrestle War
summary: Wrestle War is a professional wrestling arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1989 on the System 16 hardware. The player controls a wrestler through a series of tournament bouts using a combination of grapples, strikes, and special moves. It featured large, well-animated character sprites.

label: Crack Down
summary: Crack Down is a top-down action arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1989 on the System 24 hardware. Two players cooperatively navigate maze-like stages, planting bombs at designated points while fighting enemies. The game was known for its strategic two-player co-op gameplay.

label: Michael Jackson's Moonwalker
summary: Michael Jackson's Moonwalker is a beat 'em up arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1990 on the System 18 hardware. Up to three players control Michael Jackson as he rescues kidnapped children using dance-based magic attacks. The game featured digitized versions of Jackson's music including Smooth Criminal and Beat It.

label: GP Rider
summary: GP Rider is a motorcycle racing arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1990 on the System 16 hardware. A spiritual successor to Hang-On, the player races on Grand Prix circuits with pseudo-3D scaling effects. The game supported linked cabinets for head-to-head multiplayer racing.

label: Laser Ghost
summary: Laser Ghost is a light gun shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1990 on the System 16 hardware. Up to three players use light guns to shoot ghosts and supernatural enemies while escorting a kidnapped girl through haunted environments. It combined horror themes with cooperative shooting gameplay.

label: Bloxeed
summary: Bloxeed is a puzzle arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1990 on the System C hardware. An enhanced variant of Tetris, it added power-up blocks with special abilities like bombs and line-clearing effects. Bloxeed was one of several Tetris-inspired games Sega produced during the puzzle game boom.

label: Puyo Puyo
summary: Puyo Puyo is a puzzle arcade game developed by Compile and published by Sega in 1992 on the System C hardware. Players match falling colored blobs (puyos) in groups of four or more to clear them, sending garbage blocks to the opponent. It launched one of the most successful puzzle game franchises in Japan.

label: Rail Chase
summary: Rail Chase is a rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM3 and released in 1991 on the System 32 hardware. Players ride a mine cart on rails through a jungle/temple environment, shooting enemies with mounted guns. The game used sprite-scaling technology to create a fast-moving on-rails experience.

label: Spider-Man: The Video Game
summary: Spider-Man: The Video Game is a beat 'em up arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1991 on the System 32 hardware. Up to four players choose from Spider-Man, Black Cat, Hawkeye, and Sub-Mariner to battle through stages based on Marvel Comics storylines. The game alternated between side-scrolling beat 'em up and platform shooting sections.

label: Arabian Fight
summary: Arabian Fight is a beat 'em up arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1992 on the System 32 hardware. Up to four players fight through Arabian Nights-themed stages using swords and magic. The game was notable for its large, detailed character sprites and scaling effects.

label: Alien³: The Gun
summary: Alien³: The Gun is a light gun shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1993 on the System 32 hardware. Based on the Alien 3 film, up to two players use mounted guns to fight xenomorphs through prison colony and alien hive environments. It was a popular arcade shooter known for its intense action.

label: Golden Axe: The Duel
summary: Golden Axe: The Duel is a fighting arcade game developed and released by Sega in 1994 on the ST-V hardware. A spin-off of the Golden Axe series, it transformed the beat 'em up franchise into a one-on-one 2D fighter with weapon-based combat. The game featured characters set in the Golden Axe fantasy universe.

label: Puyo Puyo Tsu
summary: Puyo Puyo Tsu (Puyo Puyo 2) is a puzzle arcade game developed by Compile and published by Sega in 1994 on the System C hardware. It introduced the offset rule allowing players to counter incoming garbage blocks, adding strategic depth that made it the definitive competitive Puyo Puyo entry. It remains the most popular version in Japanese tournaments.

label: Wing War
summary: Wing War is a combat flight arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 1994 on the Model 1 hardware. Players pilot fighter planes in aerial dogfights using the same 3D polygon technology that powered Virtua Racing and Virtua Fighter. The game supported linked cabinets for multiplayer dogfighting.

label: Puyo Puyo Sun
summary: Puyo Puyo Sun (Puyo Puyo 3) is a puzzle arcade game developed by Compile and published by Sega in 1996 on the ST-V hardware. It introduced Sun Puyos — special blocks that add bonus garbage when cleared — along with a new story mode and updated visuals. The game continued the competitive Puyo Puyo formula.

label: Virtua Fighter Kids
summary: Virtua Fighter Kids is a fighting arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 1996 on the ST-V hardware. A comical spin-off of Virtua Fighter 2, it features super-deformed (chibi) versions of the VF2 cast with oversized heads and exaggerated animations. Despite its lighthearted appearance, the game retained the full Virtua Fighter 2 fighting engine.

label: Virtua Striker 2
summary: Virtua Striker 2 is a soccer arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 1997 on the Model 3 hardware. The sequel to Sega's first 3D soccer game, it featured improved graphics, more teams, and refined gameplay. It was widely deployed in arcades internationally and ported to the Dreamcast.

label: Top Skater
summary: Top Skater is a skateboarding sports arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 1997 on the Model 2 hardware. The player stands on a skateboard-shaped controller and performs tricks while navigating downhill courses. It was a precursor to the extreme sports arcade genre and predated Tony Hawk's Pro Skater by two years.

label: The Lost World: Jurassic Park
summary: The Lost World: Jurassic Park is a light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM3 and released in 1997 on the Model 3 hardware. Based on the film of the same name, two players use mounted guns to battle dinosaurs across jungle, city, and laboratory environments. It was one of the most popular light gun games of the late 1990s.

label: Star Wars Trilogy Arcade
summary: Star Wars Trilogy Arcade is a rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 1998 on the Model 3 hardware. The game recreates key battles from the original Star Wars trilogy, including the Death Star trench run, Battle of Hoth, and lightsaber duels. It was one of the most technically impressive arcade games of its era.

label: L.A. Machineguns
summary: L.A. Machineguns: Rage of the Machines is a rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 and released in 1998 on the Model 3 hardware. Set in a futuristic Los Angeles overrun by machines, players use mounted machine guns to destroy hordes of robotic enemies. The game was known for its fast-paced on-rails action.

label: F355 Challenge
summary: F355 Challenge is a racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 1999 on the Model 3 hardware. Players race a Ferrari F355 on licensed real-world circuits with a strong emphasis on realistic driving simulation. Designed by Yu Suzuki, it featured a high-end three-screen cabinet for an immersive cockpit experience.

label: Sega Bass Fishing
summary: Sega Bass Fishing is a sports arcade game developed by Sega AM1 and released in 1998 on the NAOMI hardware. Using a fishing rod controller peripheral, the player casts lines and catches bass in various lake environments. It was ported to the Dreamcast and became one of the console's popular titles.

label: Fighting Vipers 2
summary: Fighting Vipers 2 is a 3D fighting arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 1998 on the NAOMI hardware. A sequel to Fighting Vipers, it continued the armor-breaking combat system where players wear destructible protective gear. The game was ported to the Dreamcast.

label: Zombie Revenge
summary: Zombie Revenge is a beat 'em up arcade game developed by Sega AM1 and released in 1999 on the NAOMI hardware. A spin-off of The House of the Dead series, up to three players battle through zombie-infested environments using melee weapons, firearms, and special attacks. The game was ported to the Dreamcast.

label: The Typing of the Dead
summary: The Typing of the Dead is a typing/shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 and released in 1999 on the NAOMI hardware. Based on The House of the Dead 2, players defeat zombies by quickly typing words and phrases on a keyboard instead of shooting. The game became a cult classic for its absurd premise and educational typing practice.

label: Eighteen Wheeler: American Pro Trucker
summary: Eighteen Wheeler: American Pro Trucker is a racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 2000 on the NAOMI hardware. Players drive an 18-wheeler semi-truck across American highways, delivering cargo against a time limit while competing against rival truckers. The game featured a large truck-style cabinet with steering wheel and gear shift.

label: Outtrigger
summary: Outtrigger is a third-person shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 2001 on the NAOMI hardware. Players compete in fast-paced arena battles using various weapons in a team-based online multiplayer format. The arcade version supported network play between cabinets.

label: Beach Spikers
summary: Beach Spikers is a beach volleyball sports arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 2001 on the NAOMI 2 hardware. Players control two-person volleyball teams in arcade-style matches on sandy courts. The game was praised for its accessible controls and competitive multiplayer, and was ported to the GameCube.

label: Planet Harriers
summary: Planet Harriers is a rail shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 2001 on the Sega Hikaru hardware. A spiritual successor to Space Harrier, the game featured third-person on-rails shooting across multiple planets with advanced 3D graphics powered by the Hikaru board's phong shading capabilities.

label: World Club Champion Football
summary: World Club Champion Football (WCCF) is a collectible card-based soccer arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2002 on the NAOMI hardware. Players build and manage football teams using physical trading cards placed on a touch-sensitive field panel. WCCF became one of the most profitable arcade franchises in Japan, running through multiple seasonal updates.

label: Puyo Puyo Fever
summary: Puyo Puyo Fever is a puzzle arcade game developed by Sonic Team and released by Sega in 2004 on the NAOMI hardware. The first Puyo Puyo game developed in-house by Sega after acquiring the IP from Compile, it introduced Fever Mode chains and a new cast of characters. It was ported to numerous platforms including Dreamcast, PS2, and PSP.

label: Ghost Squad
summary: Ghost Squad is a light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 2004 on the Chihiro hardware. Players join an elite counter-terrorism unit, completing missions with branching paths and multiple objectives. The game featured replayability through mission variations and was ported to the Nintendo Wii.

label: OutRun 2 SP
summary: OutRun 2 SP (Special Tours) is a racing arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and released in 2004 on the Chihiro hardware. An enhanced version of OutRun 2, it added new courses, cars, and gameplay modes while retaining the series' signature blue-sky driving experience. It was widely regarded as one of the best arcade racers of the 2000s.

label: Sangokushi Taisen
summary: Sangokushi Taisen (Sengoku War) is a real-time card strategy arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2005 on the Lindbergh hardware. Players use physical trading cards representing Three Kingdoms-era generals, placing and moving them on a touch-sensitive game board. The franchise became one of Sega's most successful modern arcade properties in Japan.

label: Virtua Tennis 3
summary: Virtua Tennis 3 is a tennis sports arcade game developed by Sega AM3 and released in 2006 on the Lindbergh hardware. Featuring licensed professional players and improved graphics over its predecessors, it offered arcade-style tennis with accessible controls. The game was ported to PS3, Xbox 360, and PSP.

label: Rambo
summary: Rambo is a light gun shooter arcade game developed by Sega AM1 and released in 2008 on the Lindbergh hardware. Based on the Rambo film series, the player uses a mounted machine gun to fight through scenes inspired by Rambo: First Blood Part II, Rambo III, and Rambo (2008). It featured destructible environments and intense action sequences.

label: Sega Rally 3
summary: Sega Rally 3 is a rally racing arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2008 on the Europa-R hardware. The third mainline entry in the Sega Rally series, it featured multiple rally circuits with dynamic surface deformation. The budget Europa-R hardware made deployment more affordable for arcade operators.

label: Sega Race TV
summary: Sega Race TV is a stock car racing arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2008 on the Europa-R hardware. Featuring a television broadcast presentation style, the game offered arcade-style NASCAR-inspired racing with dramatic camera angles and commentary. It was one of the last dedicated racing arcade cabinets from Sega.

label: Mushiking: King of the Beetles
summary: Mushiking: King of the Beetles is a collectible card battling arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2003 on the NAOMI hardware. Children collect physical beetle trading cards and scan them to battle giant insects in the arcade machine. Mushiking became a phenomenon in Japan, selling over 500 million cards and inspiring an anime series.

label: Oshare Majo: Love and Berry
summary: Oshare Majo: Love and Berry is a collectible card rhythm arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2004 on the NAOMI hardware. Targeted at young girls, players collect fashion trading cards and scan them to dress their characters and perform dance routines. It was a massive hit in Japan, becoming the female-audience counterpart to Mushiking.

label: Kantai Collection Arcade
summary: Kantai Collection Arcade is a collectible card strategy arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2016 on the Nu hardware. Based on the popular Kantai Collection browser game, players collect physical cards representing anthropomorphized warships and command fleets in naval battles. The arcade version added 3D graphics and physical card collection mechanics.

label: Border Break
summary: Border Break is a third-person shooter arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2009 on the RingEdge hardware. Players pilot customizable mecha in team-based online battles, capturing bases and destroying enemy units. The game ran as a continuously updated service title and was later adapted for PlayStation 4.

label: Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade
summary: Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade is a rhythm arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2010 on the RingEdge hardware. Based on the popular Vocaloid character Hatsune Miku, players hit notes in time with Vocaloid music tracks. The arcade version featured continuously updated song lists and became one of the most successful rhythm arcade games in Japan.

label: Maimai
summary: Maimai is a rhythm arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2012 on the RingEdge 2 hardware. The game uses a unique circular washing machine-shaped cabinet where players tap, hold, and slide notes on a round touch screen. Maimai became one of Sega's most popular modern arcade franchises, receiving regular content updates.

label: Chunithm
summary: Chunithm is a rhythm arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2015 on the Nu hardware. Players interact with a ground slider and an air sensor, tapping and raising their hands to hit notes. Together with Maimai and Ongeki, Chunithm forms Sega's modern trio of rhythm arcade games that dominate Japanese arcades.

label: Puyo Puyo Tetris
summary: Puyo Puyo Tetris is a puzzle arcade game developed by Sonic Team and released by Sega in 2014 on the Nu hardware. The game combines two iconic puzzle franchises, allowing players to compete using either Puyo Puyo or Tetris rules — or both simultaneously in Fusion mode. It was a critical and commercial success, later ported to numerous home platforms.

label: Ongeki
summary: Ongeki is a rhythm and card-collecting arcade game developed and released by Sega in 2018 on the Nu hardware. Combining rhythm gameplay with a card-based character system, players hit notes while using a lever for movement and attacks. It is the newest entry in Sega's modern rhythm game lineup alongside Maimai and Chunithm.

label: Noriyoshi Ohba
summary: Noriyoshi Ohba is a Japanese video game developer who headed Sega's Overworks division (formerly AM7). When Overworks merged with Wow Entertainment in 2004, Ohba served as vice president of the resulting Sega Wow entity in the AM1 lineage.

label: Makoto Uchida
summary: Makoto Uchida is a Japanese video game director who worked at Sega AM1. He directed Golden Axe and Altered Beast, two landmark Sega arcade titles from the late 1980s.
notableRoles: Director of Golden Axe and Altered Beast

label: Hayao Nakayama
summary: Hayao Nakayama was a Japanese businessman who served as president of Sega Enterprises from 1984 to 1999. Under his leadership, Sega became one of the world's leading arcade and console game companies, launching the Sega Genesis/Mega Drive and overseeing the development of iconic arcade franchises. He was instrumental in Sega's golden age of arcade hardware innovation.

label: David Rosen
summary: David Rosen is an American businessman who co-founded Sega Enterprises. In the 1950s, he started importing coin-operated amusement machines to Japan. His company, Rosen Enterprises, merged with Service Games in 1965 to form Sega. Rosen served as CEO and was pivotal in establishing Sega as a global arcade game manufacturer.

label: Masamitsu Niitani
summary: Masamitsu Niitani, also known as Moo Niitani, is the founder of Compile and producer of the original Puyo Puyo puzzle game. After Compile went bankrupt in 2003, he founded Compile Heart.
notableRoles: Founder of Compile, producer of Puyo Puyo
